newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - Trinity reviews U.S. operations.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - Trinity reviews U.S. operations.

text.p: Leading British local newspaper group Trinity International Holdings Plc is reviewing its U.S. operations following the disposal of its Canadian unit, chief executive Philip Graf said on Wednesday.
"We're reviewing carefully what we're going to do in the U.S.," Graf told Reuters in a telephone interview, adding that all options would be considered.
Trinity reported U.S. operating profit of 3.2 million pounds in 1996 on turnover of 26 million. It noted substantial margin growth from the Pennysaver, its core Pittsburgh product.

Trinity's 1996 pre-tax profit more than doubled to 56.2 million pounds as the benefits of the acquisition of a number of British local papers early in the year paid off. The profit included an exceptional gain of 5.7 million stg on the sale of its Canadian newspapers to David Black in December.
Graf said 1997 had started well thanks to stable newsprint prices and good advertising growth.
He said the company's total newsprint bill including the U.S. was 50 million stg annually and noted that prices had fallen some 20 percent from their 1996 peaks.

Graf said some of the newsprint savings would be ploughed back into promotional activity and editorial development at Trinity titles, which include the Liverpool Echo, the Western Mail and the Belfast Telegraph.
Graf noted that underlying earnings growth of 15 percent had been achieved while Trinity was integrating the UK papers it bought from Canada's Thomson Corp in a 327 million stg deal last January.
Trinity shares had added 15p to 503.5p by 0933 GMT following the figures.
